criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Primary mission (reef monitoring via fluid lensing), rationale, single-spacecraft justification, and users/operator/funding are all addressed with reasonable detail and cited literature. Slightly thin on customer detail, so not top of range.

evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.
Thus, only one satellite is required.
The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: All major requirements addressed: launch site/vehicle with rationale, SSO with full COEs, manoeuvre statement, ground station, STK access report, 5-year duration and EOL. STK screenshots and access tables provided. Weakened by internal contradictions (drag sail vs no thrusters), a typo ('low resolution... also desirable'), reliance on Wikipedia, and no software files explicitly referenced.

evidence.quote: The proposed satellite will thus use the Vega E rocket as a launch vehicle – launched from the Guiana Space Centre Spaceport.
an altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 97.7924°
An average contact duration of almost ten minutes was achieved
The most promising alternative is a ‘drag sail’

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Conclusions are specific and trace back to the analysis, including caveats about Vega E availability and alternatives. Somewhat brief and does not summarise communications/EOL outcomes quantitatively, so lower end of Accomplished.

evidence.quote: A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected although it has not been built yet.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Structure is logical with headings and executive summary, but figures lack proper figure numbers/captions (only loose text labels), bibliography is bare URLs including Wikipedia (not accepted), and some writing errors ('a Earth observation', 'for the purposed of'). Formatting inconsistent in places.

evidence.quote: STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart

requirements.where: Screenshots included; no explicit software files in appendix
Bibliography uses Wikipedia [6] and bare URLs

technical_issues.issue: Typo: 'A very high altitude would yield low resolution images which is also desirable' – should read 'not desirable'.

Contradictory reasoning: states uncontrolled descent makes sense, then says satellite is 'without thrust capability' so needs passive drag sail; also earlier says only manoeuvre occurs at EOL then says no thrusters.
Wikipedia cited as source [6], which is not accepted; references are bare URLs without titles/authors/dates.
RAAN initial value 'indicates the location of the launch facility' is loosely justified; Kourou latitude 5.05°N vs 97.79° inclination claim of two daily windows is plausible but not shown.

overall: A well-structured, mostly complete mission design for GBR reef monitoring with STK evidence and sound orbit selection. Weakened by EOL contradictions, missing formal figure labels, no software files, and Wikipedia/bare-URL referencing.

feedback.summary: Your GBR reef-monitoring mission design is well structured and addresses all major requirements: launch site/vehicle, SSO with full COEs, ground contacts, duration and EOL, supported by STK evidence. To reach the top of the rubric, resolve the EOL contradictions, add formal figure captions and software files, and replace Wikipedia/bare-URL references with proper sources.
next_steps: Resolve the EOL contradiction: you state the satellite has no thrusters yet also describe a manoeuvre at EOL; clearly state whether deorbit is passive (drag sail) or active, and make the reasoning consistent throughout.

Add numbered figures with formal captions (e.g. 'Figure 1: STK 3D view of orbit, 12 hours apart') and include your STK software files in an appendix, explicitly referenced in the Mission Design section.

Replace Wikipedia [6] and bare URLs with authoritative sources (titles, authors, dates) and fix typos such as 'low resolution images which is also desirable' (should be 'not desirable'), 'a Earth observation' and 'for the purposed of'.

criteria.C1: Accomplished (8/10). Your Introduction clearly covers the primary mission (fluid-lensing reef monitoring), rationale, single-spacecraft justification, and users/operator/funding with cited literature. To reach the top of the range, expand on customer detail—how CSIRO/BOM and others would actually access and use the data.
criteria.C2: Accomplished (7/10). All major requirements are addressed: Vega E from Kourou with rationale, 600 km SSO with full COE table, manoeuvre statement, ground station access (~10 min contacts), 5-year duration and EOL, with STK screenshots. To improve, resolve the thruster/drag-sail contradiction, justify the RAAN choice and the two-daily-window claim quantitatively, and include software files.
criteria.C3: Accomplished (7/10). Your conclusions are specific and trace back to the analysis, including honest caveats about Vega E availability. To strengthen, briefly summarise the communications and EOL outcomes quantitatively (contact frequency, deorbit approach) so the conclusion reflects all evidence.
criteria.C4: Adequate (5/10). Your report has a logical structure and executive summary, but figures lack formal numbers/captions, the bibliography uses Wikipedia and bare URLs, and there are writing errors. The next level requires consistent formatting, properly cited references matching the list, and polished spelling/grammar throughout.
